o1.biggest_strength: It finds all three signals and turns them into a clean budget that adds up to exactly ₹5,60,000: relaunch 'Dad's razor vs mine' with new cuts, cut the COD-trap Starter Kit, and split out women 25 to 34. A clear ASC ladder makes it runnable on Monday.
o1.biggest_mistake: The main decision line is the ₹394 break-even on Meta's count, with the attribution-adjusted ₹282 kept only as a 'safe' line, and it scales Catalog DPA 20% even though DPA is only at break-even after the haircut and already at frequency 5.2.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Set every target on the Shopify-adjusted break-even, project before-and-after profit for the new split, and add a prepaid nudge for the COD-heavy segments.

o2.biggest_strength: Every verdict rests on store-count, after-RTO profit per ad set with the working shown, and it adds a before-and-after projection (−₹1,85,300 down to about −₹63,200) plus a sized prepaid lever (₹124 per switched order, ₹201 on the starter kit).
o2.biggest_mistake: It closes the UGC test and moves its ad into ASC after only 5 days. It also asks for a sign-off on the prepaid offer and the pauses when the brief said I can't be reached.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Commit to a specific prepaid offer, give the UGC concept a fair read before merging it, and keep the creative brief in our voice and our customers' words a bit more vividly.

reason: Both make the right big calls. Output 2 judges everything on real store orders and shows what the new split does to my profit, and the prepaid lever is money I didn't see. Output 1 is a little easier to read but still leans on Meta's count.
